premises.text: Deskless workers are poorly served by current employment systems for safety, pay, and help, and employers lack structure to meet those needs
premises.evidence_span: Current employment solutions are not actually built for these workers

premises.text: SMS is the right accessible channel because deskless workers will not adopt another app
premises.evidence_span: Deskless workers don't need another application on their phone

premises.text: A two-way SMS portal auto-answers FAQs, translates widely, and lets workers reach managers for issues like training
premises.evidence_span: Our system enables access to the software, replies to FAQs automatically, translates into over 110 languages

premises.text: Auto-resolution and campaign/survey tools save manager time while giving workers quick answers
premises.evidence_span: our auto-resolution feature resolves over 95% of the inbound questions automatically

premises.text: Advanced analytics, workplace health scores, and sentiment/psychometrics surface turnover risk before workers leave
premises.evidence_span: advanced analytics showing you the workplace health score

premises.text: Reducing turnover requires mutual trust built through accessible two-way communication between employers and deskless employees
premises.evidence_span: The mutual trust is the core component of reducing turnover

value.text: A bridge that connects deskless workers and employers to improve access, engagement, and retention
value.evidence_span: Antil is reconciling employees and employers by creating a bridge between them

causal_links.evidence_span: to build trust, we first need to provide access to that communication
when these workers are not heard, they just leave
Employees with Antil get more connectivity, more access, more education, and more engagement
Overall, our goal is to improve retention across your organization

notes: FAQ/translate/job-data feature cascade folded into P3 as one SMS portal mechanism; auto-resolution and analytics split as distinct employer-side jobs. Traction and dollar savings excluded. Future SAP/API roadmap treated as vision and omitted as a premise.
